newsitem.title: USA: Remittal agency charged with money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Remittal agency charged with money laundering.

text.p: A major New York money remittal agency has been indicted in connection with a money laundering scheme involving the transfer of millions of dollars to the Dominican Republic, federal prosecutors said Wednesday.

Remesas America Oriental Inc. and five present and former employees were named in a 23-count indictment filed in Manhattan federal court. The charges grew out of a multi-state probe of RAO, which has 14 offices in New York and New Jersey.
Money remitters are financial institutions that receive money and send it to locations designated by their customers.

The indictment alleges that RAO employees accepted cash from a confidential informant and undercover law enforcement officers posing as drug dealers who wanted the money transmitted to the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Miami.

Either the informant or the undercover officers represented that the cash came from narcotics trafficking. RAO employees allegedly broke down the money into quantities under $10,000 so that the transactions would not have to be reported to the Internal Revenue Service.
The employees allegedly transmitted the cash under false names and prepared false invoices to make it appear as if the fictitious customers had brought money to RAO, prosecutors said.
